patch_description:
I took inspiration from the seed’s hardware-efficient rotation-plus-entanglement structure, but replaced its mostly local, line-based coupling pattern with a more hierarchical mixer. The key insight is that the fixed readout measures only Z expectations, so terminal phase-only layers contribute little; instead, phase rotations must be placed before non-commuting gates to matter.

The new ansatz keeps strong per-qubit entrance flexibility, then uses a butterfly-style CZ mesh to spread information across the full 8-qubit register in two hops. After that, mirrored RZ sharing acts as a compact phase conditioner, and a split CRY/CRX bridge injects directional conditional mixing along long-range pairs. Finally, parity-tied RX rotations align the latent state with the Z readout. Compared with the seed, this is a more structured and parameter-efficient classifier block with better inductive bias for binary feature re-uploading and lower risk of overfitting.
